## Description

Pink heterotrich ciliate (180–280 µm), laterally flattened, with its pigment (blepharismin) in bands
of granules between the ciliary rows and a moniliform macronucleus. It eats bacteria, flagellates and
small ciliates; large cells can become cannibal giants. Blepharismin is its photoreceptor: it
avoids sudden increases of light and gathers in shade; under intense light with O₂ it is
photodynamic and damages the cell (albino cells resist).

## In the simulation

<!-- GENERATED:presence -->
Drops: `pond` (weight 0.15), `puddle` (weight 0.15); 2 individuals in a reference drop at weight 1.
<!-- /GENERATED -->

A filter feeder with a [photophobic response](../../mechanics/behavioural-responses.md) (`step_up` of light →
`avoid`) and [photodynamic damage](../../mechanics/behavioural-responses.md#phototaxis-photophobia-and-light-damage)
paid as maintenance stress. Pigment stripes drawn. Helical swimming. Width ~35 % of the length and
thickness half the width (estimated).

## Not implemented yet

- No cannibal giants (a morph induced by crowding).
- Light thresholds are relative to the lamp, not in physical units.
- Albino strains are not available.

## Unique and shared mechanics

Shares the [phobic response mechanism (M1)](../../mechanics/behavioural-responses.md) with *Euglena* and
*Chlamydomonas*, and pigment stripes with *Stentor*. Photodynamic damage is unique to it.
